source_note: GDOS's national pomniki przyrody register (poland-gdos-pomniki-przyrody.json, CC0) gives coordinates, designation date and species only, no name, age or girth. Polish Wikipedia's 'Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie' article reproduces the city's own official registry list ('wykaz'), including street address, girth in cm and designation year per tree, joined here to the GDOS entries by their shared INSPIRE code. This is the same join used to verify the six trees delivered this pass (kra_005 to kra_010).

leads.name: The Studencka Plane
leads.reason: Verified to the same standard as kra_005 to kra_010 (register + Wikipedia's reproduction of the official list) but cut for count: a second, smaller plane would have duplicated kra_005's species inside the same cluster. Good candidate if the walk is ever split into two smaller ones. [RESOLVED 2026-08-18, delivered as kra_011: the prior pass's own reasons (cut for count / ninth-in-line / taste) are exactly the invalid reasons CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-10 ruling forbids; shipped flagged, girth recorded, age derived only where a same-species same-register comparison existed.]

leads.name: The Wadow Park Silver Linden
leads.reason: Named by krakow.pl's own 2020-era announcement (dziewietnascie_pomnikow_przyrody) as the largest-girth tree among a batch of 19 newly designated monuments, in Wadow Park. Not pursued this pass because Wadow Park's location relative to the centre was not checked and it did not fit the Planty-ring cluster; worth a dedicated look, since 559cm girth would make it larger than every tree shipped this pass, in a second, separate cluster with a tall elm (29.5m) and a wide-crowned oak (28.2 x 22.8m canopy) from the same announcement.

leads.name: French Maple on ul. [unnamed nearby street]
leads.reason: 0.54 km from centre, 454 m from any published tree; a genuinely rare species for a Krakow street tree, which would have made a strong, distinctive addition. Not pursued this pass: designated only weeks before this pass (2026-06-06), too recent to appear in the 2023-snapshot Wikipedia wykaz table used to cross-source this city's other trees, so no second independent source (address, girth, or photo) could be found in the time available. GDOS alone is one source. Worth a dedicated look once a 2026 update to the city's own wykaz or a local news item about the new designation surfaces.

leads.name: Cluster of exotic monuments in the Botanical Garden area (Ogród Botaniczny UJ vicinity)
leads.species: Hungarian Oak (Quercus frainetto), Canary Island Date Palm (Phoenix canariensis), Sago Palm (Cycas circinalis), a second Ginkgo biloba, and others
leads.reason: A second cluster roughly 1.4-1.6 km from the main Planty-ring cluster, around Al. Daszyńskiego / ul. Kopernika, likely inside or adjacent to the Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden, which is PAID ENTRY. Not investigated this pass beyond noting the location: worth checking who owns each individual tree's exact spot, since some (the Hungarian oak, the ginkgo) may stand on the public street outside the garden fence while the palm and cycad candidates are almost certainly under glass or paid grounds. A future pass should resolve garden-vs-street per tree before shipping any of them, per the paid-entry-share rule (at most about a third of a city behind a ticket).

blocked.name: The Muzeum Archeologiczne Red Beech
blocked.species: Common Beech, purple-leaved form (Fagus sylvatica f. purpurea)
blocked.reason: Dead. Storm-felled 17 February 2022 (Gazeta Krakowska, Nasze Miasto Krakow, RMF24, all reporting the same event); the Wikipedia registry table itself notes 'Drzewo powalone przez wichure 17 lutego 2022'. Popularly said to have been a favourite of Marshal Jozef Pilsudski, unconfirmed. A replacement sapling, the 'Drzewo Poezji' (Tree of Poetry), was planted on the same spot 21 March 2022; too young to qualify as an entry itself.

blocked.name: The Podzamcze Horse Chestnut
blocked.reason: Dead. Storm-felled 10 July 2021 per the Wikipedia registry table's own note ('Drzewo powalone przez burze 10 lipca 2021').
